body.heading: Write the alphabet
paragraphs: Write A to Z down the side of a big sheet of paper. Take it outside with your adult and start hunting with your eyes.
A is for ant or acorn. B is for bird or bark. Some letters are easy. Some letters will make you think hard.

body.heading: Hunt letter by letter
paragraphs: You do not have to go in order. When you spot something, shout its name and write it next to its letter.
Tricky letters like Q and X might need clever answers — Q for a quiet place, X for an x-shaped crossing of twigs. Clever answers count.

body.heading: Finish the sheet
paragraphs: Some days you will not find all 26 letters, and that is fine. The hunt is the game, not the finishing.
Next time, try a different place — a park, a garden, a beach. Every place hides a different alphabet.

takeaway: Hunting for the alphabet outdoors turns a walk into a word game, and every place hides different letters.
materials: Paper with the alphabet written down
safetyNotes: Look and point — you do not need to pick things up. Never taste anything you find outdoors.
screenFreeExtension: Play the alphabet game indoors with things in one room when it is raining.
